title: CameraNoise: Enabling Faithful Camera Control in Video Diffusion through Geometry-Flow-Guided Noise Warping
claim: Prior methods yield imprecise camera trajectories and appearance-entangled artifacts; ours gives accurate, appearance-agnostic control through a better motion representation.
layout: 2 stacked panels, left-to-right columns, red boxes mark baseline errors
description: The figure has two dashed-border panels stacked vertically. The top panel, 'Faithful Camera Control w/ CameraNoise', shows two cases, (a) and (b). Each has a small 3D camera-pose curve on the left, followed by three columns of stacked video frames with red anchor dots: ground truth, a baseline (MotionCtrl for case a, CameraCtrl for case b) and Ours. The baseline frames are outlined in red where the trajectory drifts, and the Ours frames match the ground truth. The bottom panel, 'Optical Flow v.s. GRFlow', shows Minecraft and Unreal Engine source motion videos for cases (c) and (d). Each is followed by an optical-flow map and generated frames #1 and #20 with red dashed boxes marking artifacts. A GRFlow map and a clean generated result are on the right. The eye goes first to the red-outlined baseline frames and the sharp final images.
caption: We highlight two key observations. (1): Shown in case (a) and (b), camera trajectories visualized by stacked frames with red anchor points show that MotionCtrl [32] and CameraCtrl [13] provide only limited precision, while our method achieves accurate control. (2): Comparing optical flow and our GRFlow for CameraNoise warping. Optical flow entangles appearance with motion, causing artifacts (red dashed boxes). By contrast, GRFlow enables appearance-agnostic generation, yielding visually correct and coherent video content. Camera motion templates are obtained from Minecraft (case (c)) and Unreal Engine (case (d)). The textual prompts for cases (c) and (d) are “Two dogs in a room” and “A monkey in the water”, respectively.
abstract: Precise camera pose control is critical for video diffusion, yet maintaining geometric consistency remains a challenge. Existing methods that directly inject numerical camera parameters into the diffusion backbone often fail to bridge the gap between abstract coordinates and visual content, leading to structural distortions. To address this issue, we propose CameraNoise, a flow-to-noise warping method that encodes camera motion into a temporally coherent stochastic representation. Unlike conventional conditioning, CameraNoise embeds camera poses directly into the noise space. This decouples motion from scene appearance while faithfully preserving trajectory dynamics. Specifically, we introduce a novel Geometry-guided Reprojection Flow and a noise warping algorithm, which jointly preserve the Gaussian prior of diffusion and ensure consistent noise propagation under camera transformations. By integrating CameraNoise into the diffusion process, our framework delivers stable, high-fidelity videos. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our approach significantly outperforms prior methods in both visual quality and trajectory faithfulness. The project page and code are available at: https://gulucaptain.github.io/CameraNoise/.
